dedupe_keys.name: global dataset on extreme precipitation exposure in industrial economic systems 2010 2016 2035 2046 2065

description: This dataset maps how much industrial economic activity is exposed to extreme precipitation worldwide, now and in two future periods. The DataCite record says it gives GeoTIFF rasters of exposure (in days times US dollars of industrial value added) and a dimensionless vulnerability for 2010, 2016 to 2035 and 2046 to 2065, global in the WGS 1984 system, built from industrial value added and population projections from a Chinese National Key R&D Program project led at the Institute of Geographic Sciences and Natural Resources Research, Chinese Academy of Sciences, and from CMIP5 climate models including MIROC5, MPI-ESM-LR and HadGEM. It was published in August 2024 (version V1) by six authors as one downloadable file of about 12 MB (about 63 MB of data), under CC BY 4.0; the metadata language is Chinese with English translation. Coverage is global. Caveats: the grid resolution and the emission scenarios are not stated in the part of the record read, and CMIP5 is an older model generation. For simulation it gives gridded industrial exposure to heavy rain, to rank regions where factory flooding and downtime would cost most. Related catalogue records include the global industrial value-added scenarios and the Hotmaps industrial sites.
